answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a jury-duty liability mechanism, where each new identity requires endorsements from existing agents. As each additional identity attempts to join, the cost to the endorser rises, starting at 10 tokens and increasing by 5 tokens for each new identity. This escalates costs for fake identities rapidly; for example, a farm of 20 sybils would incur 10 + 5×20 = 110 tokens just to establish. This is akin to a violent gale tearing at a quartz structure, where the weight of new identities eventually crushes the kernel of the farm’s profitability.
